parts.title: How I became a cartoonist
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was eleven, I was too shy to talk in class, so I started drawing small pictures in my notebook instead. My drawings were about a rabbit called Max, who gets into trouble wherever he goes. My friends loved them, and soon they were asking me for a new story every week.

Last year, my art teacher suggested that I put the comics online. I was afraid at first, because anyone in the world could see them. In the end, I made a simple website, and I wrote a short story to go with each picture. I got only five readers in the first month, and four of them were my relatives.

Then something unexpected happened. A famous cartoonist saw my comic and shared it with his followers. By the next morning, over three thousand people had visited my site. I could hardly believe it.

I am still at school, and drawing takes up many of my evenings, but I do not mind. My dream is to become a professional cartoonist, and I try to draw something every day, even when I am tired.

parts.title: How a cartoon film is made
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Making a cartoon film takes a great deal of time and many people. [1] Writers decide what will happen and in which order, and artists make simple drawings of each scene.

Next, the artists create the characters. [2] A character must look the same from the front, from the side and from behind, so that the audience always recognises it.

Then comes the animation. In the past, artists drew thousands of pictures by hand. [3] Today, most of the work is done on computers, which saves months of effort.

Voices are recorded separately. [4] The actors often read their lines in a small room with a microphone, and they sometimes watch the drawings while they speak.

Finally, music and sound are added. [5] A single minute of a film can take several weeks to finish.
sentences: They try out many different faces, clothes and colours.
Many cartoon characters are later sold as toys.
This is often done before the pictures are finished.
Each picture was only slightly different from the one before.
All of this work needs a lot of patience.

gaps.explanation: The story comes first; the next sentence says writers decide what will happen.
The artists create the characters and try out faces, clothes and colours; then a character must always look the same.
Artists drew thousands of pictures by hand, each slightly different, before computers.
Voices are recorded before the pictures are finished; the next sentence is about the actors.
All this work needs patience; the next sentence says one minute can take weeks.

parts.title: A short history of comics
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Comics have been popular [1] more than a hundred years. The first ones appeared in newspapers, where they were printed in black and white. [2] 1938, a new kind of hero appeared who could fly, and sales increased very quickly. [3] then, thousands of different characters have been created. Some stories are funny, [4] others are serious or scary. Today, many people read comics on their phones instead [5] buying them in shops. However, printed comics have not disappeared. Old copies can [6] worth thousands of pounds.

gaps.explanation: For is used with a period of time: for more than a hundred years.
In is used with a year: in 1938.
Since then means from that time until now.
The sentence contrasts two kinds of story.
Instead of is followed by the -ing form.
Can be worth: modal verb followed by the infinitive.

parts.title: A cartoon workshop
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: cartoonist
turns.text: Hello, everyone. My name is Olin, and I have been a cartoonist for twelve years. Today's workshop is about drawing a funny face. First, you need a pencil, not a pen, because you will make mistakes. Start with a circle for the head. Then add two big eyes, because large eyes make a face look friendly. Do not forget the eyebrows. They are the best way to show feelings, so try to make them move up and down in your drawing. Next, draw a large mouth. A wide smile looks happy, and a small straight line looks bored. After that, you can use a black pen to go over your pencil lines. Wait until it is dry, and then rub out the pencil. Finally, colour your picture with bright markers. The workshop finishes at four, and you can take your picture home.

gaps.explanation: He says he has been a cartoonist for twelve years.

gaps.explanation: He says you need a pencil, not a pen.

gaps.explanation: He says large eyes make a face look friendly.

gaps.prompt: The best way to show feelings is with the ___
gaps.explanation: He says the eyebrows are the best way to show feelings.

parts.title: An interview with a webcomic artist
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Kendal, you draw a popular online comic. How did it begin?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I drew it during boring lessons at university. I did not plan to show anyone, but my flatmate persuaded me to put one page online.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How often do you post new pages?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Twice a week, on Tuesdays and Fridays. I plan the story months in advance, but I draw each page in about eight hours.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Where do you get your ideas?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: From ordinary life. The funniest things happen on trains and in cafes. I always carry a small notebook.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do your readers ever disagree with you?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: All the time! Last year I changed a character's name after hundreds of readers told me they hated it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Is it difficult to earn money from comics?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: In the beginning, yes. I worked in a shop for three years. Now I earn enough from my readers and from selling books, so I draw full time.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What would you say to someone who wants to start?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Draw something every day, even if it is bad. Your own style only appears after a lot of practice.
